{
  "candidate_rtl": "module pw_fsm_sync (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input start,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg done
);

localparam [8:0] S_IDLE  = 9'b000000001;
localparam [8:0] S_START = 9'b000000010;
localparam [8:0] S_READ  = 9'b000000100;
localparam [8:0] S_PROC1 = 9'b000001000;
localparam [8:0] S_PROC2 = 9'b000010000;
localparam [8:0] S_PROC3 = 9'b000100000;
localparam [8:0] S_WAIT  = 9'b001000000;
localparam [8:0] S_DONE  = 9'b010000000;
localparam [8:0] S_ERROR = 9'b100000000;

reg [8:0] state, next_state;

always @(*) begin
    next_state = S_IDLE;
    case (state)
        S_IDLE:  next_state = start ? S_START : S_IDLE;
        S_START: next_state = data_in[0] ? S_READ : S_ERROR;
        S_READ:  next_state = (data_in[3:1] == 3'b101) ? S_PROC1 : S_WAIT;
        S_PROC1: next_state = S_PROC2;
        S_PROC2: next_state = data_in[7] ? S_PROC3 : S_WAIT;
        S_PROC3: next_state = S_DONE;
        S_WAIT:  next_state = data_in[4] ? S_READ : S_WAIT;
        S_DONE:  next_state = S_IDLE;
        S_ERROR: next_state = (data_in[2:0] == 3'b111) ? S_IDLE : S_ERROR;
        default: next_state = S_IDLE;
    endcase
end

wire select_read = (state == S_READ);
wire select_proc1 = (state == S_PROC1);
wire select_proc2 = (state == S_PROC2);
wire select_proc3 = (state == S_PROC3);
wire select_done = (state == S_DONE);
wire select_error = (state == S_ERROR);
wire select_pass = select_read | select_done;

// Increment carries are independent prefix reductions, not a ripple chain.
wire [7:0] incremented;
assign incremented[0] = ~data_in[0];
assign incremented[1] = data_in[1] ^ data_in[0];
assign incremented[2] = data_in[2] ^ (&data_in[1:0]);
assign incremented[3] = data_in[3] ^ (&data_in[2:0]);
assign incremented[4] = data_in[4] ^ (&data_in[3:0]);
assign incremented[5] = data_in[5] ^ (&data_in[4:0]);
assign incremented[6] = data_in[6] ^ (&data_in[5:0]);
assign incremented[7] = data_in[7] ^ (&data_in[6:0]);

always @(*) begin
    data_out = ({8{select_pass}} & data_in)
             | ({8{select_proc1}} & incremented)
             | ({8{select_proc2}} & {data_in[6:0], 1'b0})
             | ({8{select_proc3}} & ~data_in)
             | ({8{select_error}} & 8'hEE);
    done = select_done;
end

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rst)
        state <= S_IDLE;
    else
        state <= next_state;
end

endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "The targeted combinational path is the PROC1 increment followed by output selection. An inferred incrementer can introduce a carry-dependent path to the upper output bits; state decoding and output selection add delay after that arithmetic.",
  "rewrite": "Express the eight-bit increment using explicit prefix-reduction carries and XORs. Replace the output case with mutually exclusive masked terms, combining READ and DONE into one pass-through term. Preserve the original state register, state encodings, next-state case, and synchronous reset.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The prefix expressions expose balanced carry reduction opportunities and the output terms expose parallel selection, potentially improving setup WNS if increment-and-select is critical. No numerical improvement is claimed without synthesis and STA under the specified mapping and interface constraints.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Prefix reductions can trade additional logic or fanout for shorter carry depth. Common subexpression sharing and mapping determine the final area. The 1102.432320um2 cap and electrical limits require evaluation; they have not been measured here. No registers, latency, or helper modules are added.",
  "functional_boundaries": "All state transitions, synchronous reset behavior, named state encodings, and output timing are unchanged. Increment overflow remains truncated to eight bits. Exact equality decoding preserves zero outputs for every unrecognized defined state, and the original default transition to IDLE remains intact. There are no initialization dependencies, assumptions, latches, memories, generated clocks, or undefined output assignments."
}
